title: Correct average acceleration magnitude
description: Essential Criteria: The student must calculate the magnitude of average acceleration as 300 m/s² using the correct change in velocity and time interval.

title: Correct acceleration direction
description: Important Criteria: The student must state or imply that the acceleration direction is west, consistent with the velocity change from east to west.

title: Correct time on grass
description: Essential Criteria: The student must calculate the time the ball moves on the grass as 10 s using the appropriate kinematic equation.

title: Proper velocity change calculation
description: Important Criteria: The student must correctly compute Δv = v_final - v_initial, accounting for the opposite directions (east vs. west).

title: Correct kinematic equation application
description: Important Criteria: The student must apply v_f = v_i + a t (or equivalent) with proper signs for the deceleration phase on the grass.

title: Sign error in velocity change
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student treats velocities as scalars and computes Δv = 20 - 10 = 10 m/s, ignoring direction.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional Criteria: The student maintains consistent units (m/s, s, m/s²) throughout the calculations.
